descriptionChirho: To be pronounced or reckoned righteous before God, the forensic-soteriological passive found throughout Paul's epistles describing divine acquittal of sinners through faith.
To pronounce or reckon someone righteous, with God as the acting subject who justifies the ungodly or those who believe.
To show or acknowledge someone or something as right or just, as when wisdom is vindicated by her deeds or when people acknowledge God as righteous.
To attempt to declare or prove oneself righteous, often with a negative connotation of self-righteous pretension.
